nodes.label: Restricted NSL Submap
nodes.summary: All NSL-specific procedural deviations from ordinary criminal procedure.

nodes.label: NSL Overview — Separate Procedural Regime
nodes.summary: National Security Law (NSL) creates a separate procedural regime with: designated judges, special bail rules, restricted legal representation, no jury for certain offences, enhanced search/seizure powers.

nodes.label: NSL Bail — Article 42 and Implementation Rule 3
nodes.summary: Bail shall not be granted unless judge satisfied no risk of national security danger (NSL Art.42, Implementation Rule 3). Higher threshold than ordinary bail under Cap 221 s.9D.

nodes.label: NSL Search and Seizure — Implementation Rules 5-7
nodes.summary: Broader search and seizure powers under NSL Implementation Rules 5-7, allowing search without warrant in certain national security cases.

nodes.label: Designated Judges — NSL Article 44
nodes.summary: NSL Art.44: Chief Executive designates judges to handle national security cases. Only designated judges may hear NSL cases.

nodes.label: National Security Law Article 44
nodes.summary: Chief Executive designates judges to handle national security cases.

nodes.label: NSL — Overseas Lawyers (Cap 159 s.27A)
nodes.summary: Overseas lawyers need Chief Executive certificate under Cap 159 s.27A to practice in NSL cases.

nodes.label: No Jury for Certain NSL Offences — NSL Article 46
nodes.summary: NSL Art.46: Certain NSL offences may be tried without a jury. Trial by three designated judges instead.

nodes.label: National Security Law Article 46
nodes.summary: Certain NSL offences may be tried without a jury; three designated judges instead.

nodes.label: NSL — Enhanced Interception and Covert Surveillance Powers
nodes.summary: NSL Implementation Rules provide enhanced interception and covert surveillance powers beyond ordinary regime.

nodes.label: Key NSL Case Seeds
nodes.summary: HKSAR v Lai Chee Ying (2021) 24 HKCFAR 121 — no jurisdiction to review NPC/NPCSC acts. Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police [2020] — journalistic material search. HKSAR v Lai Man Ling [2021] HKCFA 28 — NSL evidence-gathering powers.
